label: Second copy step (recall_idx 1) in length-9 sequences
explanation: Purely positional/length feature. Fires only in the copy phase, at the step right after <DEL> (t = L+1, input = first original token, output = second original token). 99.98% of activations are at recall_idx 1; 93% of activation mass is in length-9 sequences (t = 10), where it fires on about 72% of sequences. Length-8 sequences (t = 9) give weak activations (~12% of sequences, 7% of mass), and it is essentially silent for L <= 7, in the original and delimiter phases, and at every other copy position. Token identity has little effect: per-token lifts are flat, and conditioning on digit/vowel/repeated tokens did not raise precision. The predicate misses the weak L=8 firings and over-predicts on the ~28% of L=9 sequences where it stays silent; I found no token-level rule that separates those.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: d, l, i, b, s, v; least: 1, t, p, -) and the current input token (most: z, 3, m, a, r, j; least: w, s, <DEL>, l); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=10, recall_idx=1, L=8 & t=9.
